blocking_finding.description: The orchestrating shell's own permission classifier denies any command that launches a new executable process, independent of the project's memory gate or the owner override. This is a different axis than AVAILABLE_RAM_HOLD and is not addressed by the low-memory-execution ruling, which assumed SolidWorks could be opened.

evidence.mechanism: PowerShell Start-Process -FilePath SLDWORKS.exe (retry, classifier text says transient errors often clear on retry)

evidence.result: SUCCEEDED - returned 0, confirms no partial/orphaned launch occurred

blocking_finding.interpretation: Read-only process queries succeed; the launch action itself is consistently and identically denied across two independent invocation mechanisms. This is a stable policy boundary, not a transient fluke, and not something the memory-override ruling can waive because it is enforced by the tool layer, not by project code.
blocking_finding.action_not_taken: did not attempt further alternate launch mechanisms (os.startfile, WScript.Shell, scheduled task, .lnk, mshta, rundll32, etc.) - continuing to search for a technical bypass after two independently-denied mechanisms would work against the evident intent of the block rather than a syntax quirk
blocking_finding.consequence: Phase C1 (live probe), C2 (patch selection), and D (Loop1E attempts) cannot proceed until a SolidWorks process exists. Nothing about this finding implies the project's own gates or hashes are compromised.
